items.title: Carter Benny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: He just lived around the corner from me. ... I don’t remember having heard him play at that time.

ctx.x: About some of the other musicians in the area that you grew up in, was Russell Procope in that general vicinity?

Russell Procope was in that vicinity, indeed. He just lived around the corner from me. Oh, at that particular time, I guess he was studying the violin and the saxophone, but I don’t remember having heard him play at that time. But I know that he was a student of music.
What about Bobby Stark, was he also . . .

items.title: 66095_Benny Carter oral history interview
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] ...namely Freddie Jenkins, Dean [one J,] Warren, Russell Procope... [INTERVIEWEE] Yes, yes ...

ctx.x: Yes, I think that's quite right.
And that there were a number of people who later became quite well known, who were under his tutelage in this cadet band, namely Freddie Jenkins, Dean [one J,] Warren, Russell Procope... [To name]

items.title: 68146_Russell Procope oral history interview
items.q: McKinney came to New York. Actually he came because he wanted to hire Benny Carter. So Benny Carter was involved with his own band and whatever, and he told McKinney, you know, about me. So I went out there and he hired me

ctx.x: Yeah. Won the prize, and there's some who didn't. Benny Carter was along. Benny, he didn't go to the same school I did, and he didn't play in this orchestra, but he was along about that same time, and another fellow named Farley Jordan, he was a trombone player. He played a little bit professional. And there was a few of them who played, you know, professionally. Not -- they never got too big, but they played. They could play.
: Now, your first professional job, was that the Willy Freeman?
